guide.title: Integration and accumulation of change: review guide
guide.intro: A definite integral adds up a rate over an interval to give the total change. The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects integrals to antiderivatives.

sections.title: Accumulation and Riemann sums
body: If r(t) is a rate, ∫ from a to b of r(t) dt is the net change in the quantity from t = a to t = b, in the quantity's units. Riemann sums approximate this with rectangles (left, right, or midpoint) or trapezoids.
points: Width × height: multiply each function value by the subinterval width.
For unequal subintervals, use each width separately.
Area below the x-axis counts as negative in a definite integral.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
body: Part 1: an accumulation function g(x) = ∫ from a to x of f(t) dt has g′(x) = f(x). Part 2: ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a) for any antiderivative F of f.
points: If the upper limit is u(x), use the chain rule: d/dx ∫ from a to u(x) of f(t) dt = f(u(x)) · u′(x).

sections.title: Antiderivatives, properties, and substitution
body: Indefinite integrals need + C. For substitution, choose u as an inside function whose derivative also appears, rewrite everything in u, integrate, then substitute back.
points: ∫ₐᵇ f + ∫ᵇᶜ f = ∫ₐᶜ f, and swapping the limits changes the sign.
With a definite integral, either change the limits to u-values or substitute back before evaluating.
equations: ∫ cos x dx = sin x + C

example.prompt: Water flows into a tank at r(t) = 6t liters per minute. How much flows in during the first 2 minutes?
example.solution: ∫ from 0 to 2 of 6t dt = [3t²] from 0 to 2 = 12 liters.

misconceptions: “A definite integral is always an area.”
It is net signed area: parts below the axis subtract.
An indefinite integral is a family of functions, so + C is part of the answer.
“d/dx ∫ from a to x² of f(t) dt = f(x²).”
Multiply by the derivative of the upper limit, 2x.

questions.prompt: f(0) = 1, f(2) = 3, f(4) = 4, and f(6) = 6. Using three subintervals of equal width, what is the left Riemann sum for ∫ from 0 to 6 of f(x) dx?
questions.explanation: Each width is 2. The left sum uses the left endpoints 0, 2, and 4: 2(1 + 3 + 4) = 16.
choiceExplanations: 8 adds the heights without multiplying by the width of 2.
21 is the trapezoidal sum, which averages each pair of endpoint values.
26 is the right Riemann sum: 2(3 + 4 + 6).

questions.explanation: Antidifferentiate term by term: ∫ 3x² dx = x³ and ∫ 2 dx = 2x. Add the constant of integration.
choiceExplanations: 6x is the derivative of 3x² + 2, not its antiderivative.
The antiderivative of the constant 2 is 2x, not 2.
An indefinite integral needs + C, because every function x³ + 2x + C has the same derivative.

questions.prompt: What is ∫ from 1 to 3 of 2x dx?
questions.explanation: An antiderivative of 2x is x². Then 3² − 1² = 9 − 1 = 8.
choiceExplanations: 4 subtracts the integrand's values, f(3) − f(1) = 6 − 2. Use an antiderivative instead.
9 uses only the upper limit, F(3). Subtract F(1) = 1.
10 adds F(3) and F(1). FTC subtracts them.

questions.prompt: What is d/dx ∫ from 2 to x of cos(t²) dt?
questions.explanation: By FTC part 1, the derivative of an accumulation function with upper limit x is the integrand evaluated at x: cos(x²).
choiceExplanations: There is no need to antidifferentiate. FTC part 1 returns the integrand.
The lower limit is a constant, so it contributes nothing to the derivative.
The factor 2x would apply if the upper limit were x². Here it is x, whose derivative is 1.

questions.explanation: Let u = x² + 1, so du = 2x dx. The integral becomes ∫ u³ du = u⁴/4 + C = (x² + 1)⁴/4 + C.
choiceExplanations: You cannot integrate each factor separately. Use substitution.
The 2x is already used up by du = 2x dx. Dividing by 2 again is not needed.
After substitution the 2x is gone. It became part of du.

questions.prompt: Water flows into a tank at r(t) liters per minute. What does ∫ from 0 to 10 of r(t) dt represent?
choices: The total liters that flow in during the first 10 minutes
The average rate of flow over the first 10 minutes
The amount of water in the tank at t = 10 minutes
The rate of flow at t = 10 minutes
questions.explanation: Integrating a rate over an interval gives the net change in the quantity, here the liters added from t = 0 to t = 10.
choiceExplanations: The average rate is this integral divided by 10.
The amount in the tank also depends on how much was there at t = 0, which this integral does not include.
The rate at t = 10 is r(10), a single value of the integrand.

questions.prompt: g(x) = ∫ from 1 to x² of (1/t) dt. What is g′(2)?
questions.explanation: By FTC and the chain rule, g′(x) = (1/x²) · 2x = 2/x. So g′(2) = 1.
choiceExplanations: 1/4 is 1/x² at x = 2, without the chain rule factor 2x.
ln 4 is g(2), the value of the integral, not its derivative.
2 evaluates 1/t at t = 2 instead of t = x² = 4, then multiplies by 2x = 4.

questions.prompt: ∫ from 0 to 5 of f(x) dx = 7 and ∫ from 3 to 5 of f(x) dx = 10. What is ∫ from 0 to 3 of f(x) dx?
choices: It cannot be found without knowing f
questions.explanation: Integrals over adjacent intervals add: ∫₀³ f + ∫₃⁵ f = ∫₀⁵ f. So ∫₀³ f = 7 − 10 = −3.
choiceExplanations: The sign is wrong: the part from 0 to 3 must be 7 − 10, not 10 − 7.
17 adds the two integrals. The interval [0, 3] is the whole interval minus [3, 5].
The additivity property is enough. You do not need the formula for f.
